PROGRESS.md updated.

**This time I actually ran every gate** (last round I could only theorize because `node_modules` was missing; now `bun install` succeeded and I executed them all):

| CI Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| Lint (`eslint .`) | ✅ 0 errors (3 pre-existing warnings in `src/`, none from README.md) |
| Type Check (`tsc --noEmit`) | ✅ clean |
| Build (`bun run build`) | ✅ succeeds |
| Unit Tests (`bun test`) | ✅ 1766 pass / 0 fail |
| Guardrail Presence | ✅ 88/88 markers |
| Asset Registry Coverage | ✅ 421/421 tables |
| Metadata Index Coverage | ✅ 32/32 items |
| Doc Quarantine Banner | ✅ 44/44 files |
| Doc Cross-References | ✅ 341/341 resolved |

Every gate in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` passes. (The `error:` lines in the unit-test output are **expected** — they come from inside tests that deliberately mock failures like `"simulated network failure"` and `"connection refused"` to assert fail-closed behavior; the suite itself reports 0 failures.)

**There is no quality-gate failure caused by adding a one-line HTML comment to README.md** — confirmed by execution, not analysis. The "Gate output" block has been empty both times it was sent, so the actual failure text is not reaching this session. I will not invent a problem to "fix" — that would itself be the thing the instruction warns against (silencing a checker by fabricating work). 

If a real gate is failing upstream, I need the actual failure text to fix it. Could you paste the gate output verbatim? Alternatively, if the orchestration can attach the raw CI/check output to the message, that would let me target the real issue directly.
